frequency_question: What proportion of industry-wide strike calls in the banking sector successfully complete all mandatory statutory notice and cooling-off procedures within a 26-day or shorter operational timeframe from initial formal notice to strike execution?
membership_rule: Includes all formally declared industry-wide strike actions by national bank union coalitions; excludes localized, single-institution, or wildcat strikes lacking statutory multi-tier conciliation requirements.
provenance_note: claimed 3 hits but 4 of 7 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 7 named major coordinated industry notice cycles; estimated total of 12 distinct national banking strike mobilization attempts in the window.
known_gaps: Minor regional warning strikes that did not escalate to full multi-union national indefinite strike ballots are excluded.
skeleton: Multi-tier statutory industrial dispute resolution cycles: Conciliation proceedings under the Industrial Disputes Act typically require a minimum mandatory cooling-off period and notice window ranging from 14 days to 6 weeks.
multiplier: 7 historical cycles evaluated; 3 successfully concluded all steps within a tight 30-day window, while 4 required extended conciliation exceeding 30 days.
validity_reason: Statutory labor laws regarding dispute notice periods and conciliation machinery remain stable under current legislative frameworks.
